prize_parts.citation: For the development of targeted protein degradation, in which heterobifunctional small molecules induce proximity between a target and a ubiquitin ligase so that binding is converted into removal of the protein

statement.case_for: My preferred configuration is unchanged: B007 as a single part with Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli. The round-1 exchange sharpened the case rather than weakening it. Five members include B007 in their preferred configuration, but I do not count support; what matters is that the four who argued the mechanism all rest on the same physical principle, namely that a bifunctional molecule forms a ternary complex whose cooperativity can be measured, structurally resolved and tuned, and that this converts occupancy into removal. That is a quantitative, experimentally testable principle, and it is independent of any one target or one company, which is the standard I set for a game-changer. The credit also holds in three names with a clear logic. Crews and Deshaies conceived and first demonstrated the heterobifunctional degrader in 2001, and Ciulli supplied the VHL ligand chemistry, the crystal structures of the ternary complexes and the cooperativity framework that turned the idea into a rational design discipline. I regard Ciulli over Handa as a priority-and-contribution judgement about the new modality itself, not a judgement of fame.
statement.case_against: The honest weaknesses are unchanged and I do not think they can be argued away. First, no degrader is an approved drug as far as I can verify, so the medical consequence is still prospective; I rest the case on the chemical principle, not on a clinical endpoint, and I would want the expert report to confirm the status of the late-stage trials. Second, the 2001 PROTAC paper used peptidic, cell-impermeable molecules, so Linke is right that the decisive drug-like chemistry came later, which is exactly why Ciulli belongs in the three and why the citation must be about the principle, not about the first molecule. Third, the cereblon molecular-glue strand (Handa, Ito, Gray, Sakamoto) is a partly separate history, and a three-name cut leaves out people with real claims. A citation that is honest about this has to say induced proximity and not claim to cover every degrader.

responses.point: Aili would take Handa in the third seat so that the cereblon glue branch is inside the prize, but says he would accept Deshaies over Handa if the committee prefers a pure PROTAC citation.
responses.response: I appreciate that flexibility, and it narrows the real disagreement to one question: is this one discovery or two? My answer is that the prize-level discovery is the induced-proximity design principle, demonstrated by Crews and Deshaies and made rational by Ciulli. Handa and Ito identified the target of an existing drug, which explains why thalidomide-type glues work, but the glues were found by serendipity and then explained, not designed, so the design logic that makes this a game-changer does not originate there. I also note that a citation worded around induced proximity already encompasses the glue mechanism conceptually, without crediting it by name. I will therefore hold Crews, Deshaies, Ciulli, and I would ask Aili to say whether, on priority grounds alone, he sees any reason for Handa to displace Deshaies other than clinical visibility of cereblon-based drugs.

responses.point: Somfai asks what is new chemically in degraders, calling the bifunctional design and ligand optimisation largely medicinal chemistry on top of E3 ligase biology, and says it would be better to wait; he also defends C-N coupling as a distinct step beyond the 2010 prize.
responses.response: The challenge is fair and I take it seriously. My answer is that the chemistry that is new is the quantitative control of an induced protein-protein interface: cooperativity between target and ligase is a thermodynamic property of the ternary complex that does not exist for either binary interaction, and it can be engineered through linker and ligand design and verified in binding, kinetic and crystallographic data. That is physical organic chemistry of a new kind of object, not routine ligand optimisation. I also accept your point on C-N coupling, which moved me: you showed that amine binding, deprotonation and beta-hydride avoidance make it a different mechanistic problem from the 2010 prize, and I agree Kosugi is a precursor and not a co-originator. That makes B029 a clean and mature fallback for me. Where I still differ is timing, because a modality whose principle is confirmed across many groups and several E3 ligases is not less mature merely because the approval is pending.

responses.point: Linke, as chair, agrees the principle is confirmed independently of the clinic but asks whether a later year, after an approval, would be a better moment, and notes the 2001 paper was only a peptidic proof of concept.
responses.response: The timing question is the most honest objection to my position and I do not dismiss it. I would answer that a prize for the principle does not need an approval, and that the cost of waiting is that the discovery is credited to people who are not all getting younger while the three-name cap gets harder to meet as the field grows. But I also concede the risk: if the committee wants clinical proof, B007 is the candidate that benefits most from one more year, and I would then fall back on B052 or B029 now. On your 2001 point I agree and it shapes my citation; I deliberately wrote it around the induced-proximity principle and heterobifunctional design, so that the proof of concept (Crews, Deshaies) and the drug-like chemistry (Ciulli) are both inside it.

responses.point: Zou accepts that B007 is conceptually the more novel modality but argues that any three names are a contested cut and that the absent approval means the clinical consequence is projected; Zou prefers B029 and B052 on cleaner attribution.
responses.response: I agree that the attribution is contested, and I cannot claim otherwise. My reply is that contested is not the same as unresolvable: for the principle, the 2001 demonstration and the later structure-guided chemistry give a defensible three, whereas for B052 the clean attribution to Liu comes with the separate burden of explaining chemistry versus genome engineering after 2020. I take your evidentiary standard seriously, and by it B007 does well, because ternary-complex formation is isolated and measured rather than inferred. I would resist the view that cleaner attribution alone should decide the year; if it did, we would always prefer the narrower discovery over the more consequential one.

responses.point: Chabes moved to Liu alone for B052 and proposes a two-part prize pairing it with a Crews and Deshaies PROTAC part, dropping Ciulli to stay within three people.
responses.response: I welcome that you now agree on Liu alone, and I accept your point that the citation for B052 must be worded around the chemical conversion of the base and not around cleavage. But I do not support the two-part prize with a two-name B007, because it removes Ciulli, whose structural and cooperativity work is what made degraders a design discipline, and it leaves the committee with two achievements that are each argued as borderline on maturity or scope. I would prefer one coherent prize that I can defend in full to a pairing that dilutes the citation, which is also a worry you voice yourself. If the committee does choose a pairing, I would accept B052 with Liu alone as the second part, but with Ciulli retained in the B007 part.

uncertainties: Whether any degrader has been approved or has reached a positive pivotal readout; my knowledge of the clinical status is not current and I have not verified it.
Whether a citation worded around induced proximity is accepted by colleagues as covering the cereblon glue line without naming Handa and Ito, or whether they will see it as two discoveries.
Whether the committee will treat the absence of an approval as a reason to wait a year, in which case my fallback is B052 with Liu alone, or B029 with Buchwald and Hartwig.
statement.conflict_note: No conflict or recusal with any shortlisted candidate. My Warshel/EVB, free-energy and Uppsala ribosome connections do not touch any shortlisted ballot. I remain scientifically close to the thermodynamics of ligand binding that underlies ternary-complex cooperativity, which is familiarity with the physics and not a personal tie to any credited person. The round-1 exchange did not change this disclosure.
